**Test image observations:**
- Narrow, elongated leaf (mango) placed on a flat surface
- Still mostly green but with severely irregular, deeply notched/jagged margins
- Brown necrotic tissue along the cut/damaged edges
- Large sections of leaf margin appear to have been cut/removed, creating a ragged, serrated outline

**Reference image comparison:**

1. **Cutting_Weevil**: Shows leaves with most of the blade cut away, leaving just petioles and small triangular remnants. The progressive cutting from the margin is the same mechanism — the test image appears to be an earlier/less severe stage where the insect has notched the margins deeply but not fully stripped the leaf.

2. **Anthracnose**: Shows yellow/brown discoloration over the whole leaf with irregular necrosis — no characteristic margin-cutting pattern.

3. **Die_Back**: Shows highly curled, dried-up brown leaves with wavy irregular margins due to shrinkage/necrosis — whole leaf turns brown and curls inward. The test leaf is still green with physical cuts, not this pattern.

The deeply notched/cut margins with only brown coloration along the cut edges (not whole-leaf necrosis) strongly points to mechanical cutting by a weevil insect, matching the Cutting_Weevil class.
